review_evidence: Read the complete index page. Its sole technical warning is that Allow with NotAction grants applicable actions outside the exclusion list subject to Resource scope; AWS IAM documentation confirms this and CSPM effective-permission evaluation already handles it, with focused tests/test_peaso_privesc_audit_fixes.py. The page lists service links and tools but no separate principal-to-principal technique.

The only technique changes contact or root email. Contact mutation affects recovery data, not an IAM principal. Member root-email takeover is conditional on management/delegated context, trusted access, exact member account, new-email OTP and later root recovery; MFA and centralized root controls remain barriers. The page does not prove a usable root session from the API writes alone.

CreateToken Studio login and PassRole app-role routes are cataloged. GetToken is application-plane only; variable/log reads have no verified AWS credential. Existing-role UpdateApp/UpdateBranch build routes need branch, job-scope and code-execution evidence; marked as candidates rather than inferred role edges.

Read every technical heading: API-key creation, GET/resource-policy reads and writes, REST Lambda integration plus deployment, REST/HTTP authorizer replacement, and the VPC-link caveat. AWS PutIntegration lets API Gateway assume an integration role to call a backend; it does not issue those role credentials to the caller. Lambda authorizer policies authorize API method invocation, not general IAM actions. The page gives no controlled Lambda code or exact IAM write target that would establish another AWS principal, so no deterministic principal edge is missing from the active YAML for this page. API Gateway PutIntegration and Lambda-authorizer docs.

Read the complete page and checked AWS AppConfig external-source profile and retrieval-role documentation. CreateConfigurationProfile plus PassRole, StartDeployment and AppConfig Data reads can expose bytes fetched through a named role, but the page identifies no usable AWS credential or second principal. The role's delegated read is bounded to the configured source; no principal-to-principal edge is established.

Reviewed the full page against AWS App Runner IAM, DescribeService, deployment and ECR push documentation. CreateService/PassRole, UpdateService/PassRole and existing-role UpdateService remain cataloged. The mutable private-ECR tag route now joins the exact same-account repository and image tag, automatic deployment, mutability, all permissions needed to push a new image, and the service instance role. Plaintext environment values remain data disclosure unless a usable IAM credential and new authority are separately verified. This page adds no other principal-to-principal route.

Existing running DESKTOP fleet and both RUNNING builder role-session routes are cataloged and tested. Application launch update reviewed: exact application-to-Elastic-fleet association and fleet role are not collected together, so it remains excluded pending a scoped join. Other sections still need individual review.

Self-contained CreateGraphqlApi, schema, HTTP data source, resolver and API-key path is cataloged with exact PassRole and global setup grants. Existing API, UpdateDataSource and UpdateResolver variants need a collected callable field, data-source role and usable caller authorization. Other resolver changes are application data effects, not an exact IAM role transition.

Reviewed all four executable Spark headings. CreateWorkGroup requires one available exact workgroup name, effective CreateWorkGroup/StartSession/StartCalculationExecution and PassRole grants, and an Athena-trusting execution role; the page now states this. Existing calculation, Spark Connect endpoint and notebook URL routes use collected live session, exact role, engine/state and workgroup action scope. Focused positive and negative tests for all four routes pass; stored-query poisoning is on a separate page and remains a candidate there. AWS Athena SessionConfiguration, GetSessionEndpoint, CreatePresignedNotebookUrl and Service Authorization Reference.

Read every route. UpdatePreparedStatement and UpdateNamedQuery alter saved SQL or application data but do not establish another AWS principal or IAM permission. AWS UpdateNotebook confirms it only replaces notebook contents and requires SessionId for an active notebook; it does not run the new code. A role edge needs the exact notebook-to-workgroup execution role, executable notebook content, and a later execution trigger. CSPM currently collects a workgroup role but no notebook inventory or exact consumer event, so the retired aws-athena-updatenotebook-poison remains a candidate and its exclusion prevents a false role edge. No active YAML route is justified by this page alone.

Read the complete page: DbConnectAdmin authorizes the source IAM identity to use the cluster's database admin role, while PutClusterPolicy can grant that same identity the database connect action. AWS authentication, database-role and resource-policy docs confirm these effects are scoped to Aurora DSQL and do not yield another IAM principal. The principal-validation link is reconnaissance, not a role transition; no catalog route is missing from this page.

Read all ten headings. RegisterJobDefinition with PassRole and SubmitJob on a usable queue is active with exact role, definition and queue joins; the separate SubmitJob-only route uses a recorded ACTIVE definition revision and its fixed job role. Both have current sign-off and focused positive/negative tests. The mutable ECR-tag section is excluded as a conditional candidate under the retired ECR consumer route: the Batch definition records its image and role, but a later submission, mutable repository/tag and full push authorization must be joined before claiming execution. AWS SubmitJob, TaskContainerProperties and ECR tag-mutability documentation confirm the distinction.

CreateCodeInterpreter, CreateAgentRuntime, CreateHarness and UpdateAgentRuntime are active but still need current sign-off on generated resource scopes, code source, lifecycle and full composite permissions. Existing READY code interpreters and harnesses have collectable execution-role joins through GetCodeInterpreter/GetHarness; marked candidates until CSPM adds exact runtime/endpoint and session authorization checks. Corrected harness command example to use the underlying runtime ARN and an active session; the command response is an event stream. Prompt-injection shell route remains conditional on model behavior.

Existing Code Interpreter execution-role pivot is a collectable candidate via List/GetCodeInterpreter, READY status and exact Start/Invoke grants. CreateAgentRuntime/PassRole and Lambda action-group hijack have active entries but require current artifact, runtime and agent-to-function invocation joins for sign-off. The Lambda code-change action alone does not prove the agent will invoke that function.

The only route is CreateJob plus PassRole to a Braket-trusting role with attacker-controlled job code. The catalog now checks both device and service-generated job ARN authorization in one documented SV1 Region. A device-only, job-only or wrong-Region CreateJob grant does not give a role edge; other device scopes remain unresolved. The passed role, controlled code/S3 path and job startup remain required; focused evaluator tests cover these outcomes.

Reviewed the full page against AWS CreateBudgetAction, ExecuteBudgetAction, configuration and SsmActionDefinition docs. The SSM action accepts only STOP_EC2_INSTANCES or STOP_RDS_INSTANCES, so the page no longer claims arbitrary Command execution. An IAM policy attachment can grant an exact controlled principal new authority only after an existing budget, passable trusting role with target-scoped attach permission, crossed threshold and action execution are established. The page example now uses MANUAL approval and waits for Pending rather than suggesting ExecuteBudgetAction bypasses budget evaluation. The old full-role edge remains excluded; exact self-permission gain is a separate candidate. AWS operation mapping also lists aws-portal:ModifyBilling, with account migration nuance. The CSPM collects existing budget actions but not DescribeBudgets, so it cannot prove that an arbitrary existing budget has sufficient spend to trigger a newly created action.

Read the full Chatbot page and current AWS CreateSlackChannelConfiguration and chat permissions documentation. CreateChannelConfiguration can bind an exact passed IAM role to an authorized Slack or Teams channel, but AWS IAM permission does not identify a channel member controlled by that same caller. Channel or account user-role requirements, guardrails and unsupported chat commands further limit role use. The page states these dependencies accurately. The retired role route stays a candidate for external chat-identity and allowed-command evidence; it must not become a concrete IAM principal edge from AWS inventory alone.

The page points to Cloud Control GetResource/ListResources with an explicitly passed handler role. AWS says Cloud Control uses that role for the typed resource operation; the caller receives bounded resource output, not the role session or its IAM permissions. No second-principal edge is established.

Read the whole Cloud Control page and checked AWS CreateResource, supported resource types, IAM action mapping, and AWS::IAM::User properties. Corrected the page in HackTricks commit 4faa1d16d0: RoleArn is bounded to one supported resource operation and does not expose role credentials or authorize arbitrary resources; the concrete route creates a new IAM user with chosen login password and AdministratorAccess. Active YAML aws-cloudcontrol-passrole-createresource requires CreateResource and a passable CloudFormation-trusted role whose effective IAM actions can create and read that user, create its login profile, and grant an administrator policy; current tests cover missing password/read/action/trust and occupied name. UpdateResource on an existing resource needs an exact controlled principal and handler-specific join, so the page does not justify a generic second edge.

Reviewed stack create/update/change-set routes, both StackSet modes, nested S3 template and SSM parameter poisoning, private extension registration, CDK bootstrap and the excluded TrustedAccounts path. Eight catalog routes cover the direct service-role and extension patterns; the three retired nested-template, supplied-parameter and attached-StackSet routes remain candidates missing exact consumer and role joins. Current PassRole and StackSet routes still need a supported template effect before sign-off. Corrected the page: CreateStack accepts inline TemplateBody as well as TemplateURL. AWS CreateStack, service-role, StackSet and extension docs.

The subpage has one PassRole plus CreateStack route, already represented by aws-cloudformation-passrole-createstack. DescribeStacks only reads the new stack outputs after completion; it is not a separate escalation edge. Template-controlled IAM user/key creation remains bounded by the passed role and stack completion.

Read the complete privesc page. Distribution redirects and CloudFront Functions affect application traffic but do not run as another IAM principal. The Lambda@Edge route now covers creating a distribution as well as updating an exact existing distribution, with dual service trust, versioned function actions, PassRole and service-linked-role readiness. A new distribution needs no existing distribution inventory; scoped UpdateDistribution grants are checked against the recorded ARN. Deployment and an edge request remain conditional. AWS Lambda@Edge permissions and CloudFront service-authorization guides; focused positive and negative tests.

Read the entire page and verified GetSpaceCredentialsForOrganization, GetSpace, SpaceCredentialRequestContext and Omni IAM docs. The operation returns a one-hour member-space session to an authorized management/delegated administrator, but its response names no IAM principal and its grants need not equal the full dataAccessRoleArn. The page and exclusion avoid a role-takeover claim. The documented domainId plus targetAccountId context does not override the operation's existing-space prerequisite; no second path is asserted without authorized success evidence. CreateView/UpdateView changes telemetry visibility, not an IAM principal. The old aws_role route is excluded as a scoped credential read, not a proven principal-to-principal edge.

Read the full package-publication route and checked AWS CodeArtifact publishing and asset-overwrite rules. PublishPackageVersion can add a new scoped version, and PutPackageMetadata can affect tags, but an existing asset cannot be replaced with different bytes. A later consumer must resolve that version and execute its contents under a known role; exact pins or lockfiles may prevent selection. This page supplies no package-to-consumer dependency, future install/build trigger or exact IAM role, so publication permission alone is not a deterministic principal transition. No additional route on the page needs active YAML until those joins are recorded; AWS Packages overview and permissions reference.

Reviewed StartBuild/Batch, project creation and update, running sandbox command/connection, sandbox start, paused-build SSM, source ZIP overwrite, secret/parameter environment poisoning, RetryBuild and plaintext environment reads. Existing exact catalog routes cover buildspec override, project role passing, recorded sandbox execution and credential-content reads; the SSM paused-build route still lacks a collected live session target. Three retired input-poisoning routes remain candidates until the exact source key or environment reference, executable consumer, trigger and role are joined. RetryBuild repeats a fixed historical build and alone does not supply attacker code or a new role session. AWS CodeBuild project, sandbox and build APIs.

Reviewed the GitPush-to-pipeline, CloudFormation deploy and CodeBuild source variants against AWS CodeCommit source-action, branch-condition, trigger and CloudFormation action documentation. The configured RepositoryName and BranchName identify a source, but a role edge additionally needs effective GitPush on that exact branch, source-change detection or another run path, an artifact actually consumed by a code-executing action, and that action's exact role. The current CodeCommit-to-CodeBuild view leaves BranchWritable, BuildSpecUsesInput and ExecutionPathAvailable unknown, while CloudFormation configuration and its template/role join are missing. All three retired routes remain candidates, without treating repository push alone as a role takeover.

Reviewed Git-sync configuration and repository-link redirection against AWS CreateSyncConfiguration, UpdateSyncConfiguration and UpdateRepositoryLink APIs. Create/UpdateSyncConfiguration with PassRepository and PassRole needs control of the exact linked repository branch and deployment file before the Git-sync role can deploy an attacker-chosen template. ResourceName identifies the existing update target; the page no longer claims it is changed by that call. UpdateRepositoryLink can replace only the connection or KMS key, not the repository owner/name, and needs an existing consumer, same-provider usable connection and controlled branch/file for a principal edge. CSPM collects no repository-link, sync-configuration or external Git write witness, so both routes remain candidates.

The one documented route remains a candidate: CreateDeployment can execute a controlled lifecycle hook on a targeted EC2 host, but the catalog does not prove an attacker-controlled revision, a working target agent and exact instance profile. The CSPM has a deployment-group-to-instance role matcher; revision control and execution readiness still need a joined witness before restoring the route.

Read both credential routes and the linked CodePipeline post-exploitation descriptions. PollForJobs is limited to matching Custom action jobs; GetJobDetails requires a valid known job ID. AWS JobData and GetJobDetails document artifactCredentials as temporary STS credentials for the pipeline S3 artifacts when the job needs them. Neither page gives a stable credential subject, job availability, or additional authority from the caller permission alone, so the two retired variants remain candidates requiring an actual job and credential evidence; no exact principal-to-principal YAML edge can be inferred here. AWS PollForJobs, GetJobDetails and JobData API docs.

Reviewed the four build execution patterns, S3 source overwrite, variable injection, stage retry/transition/condition/rollback, approval, custom-job result, and PollForJobs. Three new pipeline source variants are checked in the catalog; the existing CodeBuild project route retains a source-viability gap. The two retired S3 source overwrite routes remain candidates until exact source key, downstream artifact consumer, trigger and role are joined. Start-only variables and gate/replay actions produce another role effect only when a recorded downstream action uses that input or gate; broad role edges are not justified by permission alone. AWS CodePipeline S3 source, action and stage APIs.

Reviewed full page and both linked technique pages. CreateProject with PassRole, CreateProject plus AssociateTeamMember, and CreateProjectFromTemplate were historical principal or IAM-policy paths. AWS now lists CodeStar in full shutdown, meaning its APIs are unavailable; no executable current route belongs in the catalog. AWS Services in Full Shutdown.

Reviewed full historical policy example and parent page. The project Owner path formerly generated an IAM policy for the member, but CodeStar is now in full shutdown and the project APIs are unavailable. Keep historical explanation only; no active principal-to-principal edge. AWS Services in Full Shutdown.

Reviewed full PassRole and CloudFormation toolchain path and parent page. It formerly required CodeStar CreateProject and an S3 template; CodeStar is now in full shutdown, so the required API cannot create a current role-mediated route. Keep historical explanation only; no active catalog technique. AWS Services in Full Shutdown.

Reviewed all principal-bearing sections and existing active/excluded source mappings. Four exact developer-token pivots are active: default authenticated role, Basic-flow trusted role, SetIdentityPoolRoles plus PassRole, and UpdateIdentityPool to enable Basic flow. User-pool sign-in, group, provider and session-tag paths remain tracked as candidates because token subject or exact role/policy authority is unproved. Guest access is a public exposure or a scope-down session, not an automatic full-role edge. Corrected page claims that SetIdentityPoolRoles, UpdateIdentityPool and AdminInitiateAuth alone yield another principal; AWS Cognito identity-pool flow, IAM roles and User Pools auth API docs. Added the exact UpdateIdentityPool guest Basic-flow role route: one collected pool without role mappings, same-pool update permission, public guest token and target trust for aud plus unauthenticated amr; cross-account trust is explicit. The page now distinguishes enhanced-flow session-scoped guests from Basic-flow full role credentials.

Read the complete self-service attribute page and checked AWS UpdateUserAttributes, attribute permissions and identity-pool role-mapping docs. UpdateUserAttributes uses a signed-in Cognito user access token; AWS explicitly does not evaluate IAM identity policies for this API. A writable custom claim can select an identity-pool IAM role only when the app client exposes the claim in a new ID token and an exact identity-pool rule matches it. This is a Cognito-user-to-role configuration risk, not an IAM-principal source edge, and is excluded from the IAM source graph. The page and exclusion now state the conditional role impact without claiming an exposure check exists.

Reviewed automatic and manual remediation and the PassRole variant. The active route is still not signed off: it can report a role without an eligible Config rule, noncompliant resource, usable SSM Automation document or remediation service-linked role, and wildcard resource checks can miss exact-scoped grants. Manual remediation as initiating principal is a distinct condition. Need exact Config rule/compliance/recorder and document inventory, same-rule permission joins and Automatic=true PassRole context before an executable finding. AWS Config PutRemediationConfigurations, remediation and service-linked-role docs.

The page covers tag-conditioned Cases self-permission and CreateCase tag override. Both affect the same caller on exact Cases resources and require the second action/policy condition or dependent tag permission; they do not give that caller another AWS principal. The existing scoped grant covers the bounded self-permission case.

Read all substantive Connect page routes. SAML session-name impersonation, managed-user email reset, and security-profile changes affect Connect application identities; GetFederationToken and participant tokens do not return IAM credentials. The delegated-flow reference does not establish a target IAM role. Six separate conversation or data exposure candidates remain unresolved until an actual embedded AWS credential, its principal and added authority are recorded; no IAM role edge follows from the page alone.

Read the complete Account Factory and AFC page against AWS Control Tower provisioning and blueprint docs. ProvisionProduct or UpdateProvisionedProduct alone does not prove a new AWS principal: the OU baseline, account-creation permission, resulting Identity Center user assignment and source control of that user must join. AFC needs control of the exact hub product/template, a selected target account, successful deployment and a member-account StackSet execution role allowed to create the intended IAM access. HackTricks Cloud 1a8e773ef8 now states these limits; the retired Account Factory route remains a candidate until its exact identity/account join is available.

Read all three PassRole routes and the non-path constraints. CreateIntegrationWorkflow delegates creation of integration resources, CreateSegmentSnapshot uses its role for KMS/S3 export, and AssociateStreamForSegments uses its role for KMS/Kinesis event delivery; none exposes that role or grants the caller another AWS principal. PutIntegration, CreateEventStream and GetUploadJobPath likewise do not establish a principal edge. AWS CreateSegmentSnapshot API and Customer Profiles service authorization reference confirm the bounded operations.

Read the sole route and introductory sections, and checked AWS Data Pipeline IAM roles, EC2 resource role, service availability and Service Authorization Reference. The page states that the pipeline needs both a passable pipeline role and EC2 resource role, a runnable definition and a launched instance; it does not claim role credentials from IAM grants alone. The old active YAML checked only PassRole on the EC2 role and three generic Data Pipeline actions; a new precondition now returns unknown rather than a concrete role edge until customer eligibility, both roles, pipeline authorization and the runnable launch path can be joined. The active technique still needs a positive exact implementation; no second page route was found.

Read both technical routes, the scheduled variant, and AWS CreateLocationS3, UpdateLocationS3 and task-scheduling docs. CreateLocationS3 selects a bucket, subdirectory and passed S3 access role; UpdateLocationS3 can replace that role or subdirectory but cannot change the stored bucket. A task moves selected objects under the role, including later scheduled transfers, but neither API issues the role credentials nor grants its unrelated AWS actions to the caller. The two retired aws_role targets remain excluded_verified; exact S3 disclosure or tampering is a separate bounded outcome. No principal-to-principal YAML edge is supported by these two page routes.

GetEnvironmentCredentials and AssociateEnvironmentRole can produce a role session for a project member, but the page observes a session policy that excludes role chaining. The CSPM lacks environment, membership, profile and exact role joins, and its full IAM-role target would overstate the session. Both retired routes are candidates for a bounded session model; blueprint role substitution remains service-limited provisioning. AWS DataZone APIs.

Existing queue-role and worker-role vending, including registering a worker on an existing customer-managed fleet, are cataloged and evaluated with exact resource and role joins. Direct IAM API callers do not need monitor membership. The two PassRole routes still need exact create or update joins. AWS service-role guidance limits fleet credential impact to worker operations and logs; unrelated attached permissions are not assumed effective.

Reviewed both custom-test paths and the service authorization/API documentation. The existing-project, new-web-test PassRole route now requires a collected project, a compatible project-listed device pool, exact CreateUpload and ScheduleRun grants on project/pool/generated uploads, and a passed role trusting Device Farm; positive and negative direct tests pass. AWS device pool ARNs are not children of project ARNs, so the collector uses the ListDevicePools project response to bind them. The separate existing-test-spec and UpdateUpload variants still need exact controlled upload, runnable project/device/package/spec and execution-role joins; they remain candidates without a definite edge.

Reviewed both password-reset and Management Console routes against AWS ResetUserPassword, regional console-access and directory-role assignment documentation. ResetUserPassword can reset a suitable existing user and reenable a disabled user, subject to Managed Microsoft AD OU and Simple AD privileged-group restrictions. The built-in Admin subject is a candidate for an exact directory-scoped principal target, not an account-wide administrator placeholder. An IAM role edge additionally requires the exact directory user or group assignment, enabled regional console access, an access URL and usable sign-in; the current inventory lacks this join. The two retired routes therefore remain candidates.

Reviewed the script-bearing DLM route and snapshot-sharing reference against AWS application-consistent snapshot and DLM service-role documentation. CreateLifecyclePolicy with PassRole can schedule a selected SSM Command document through the DLM role on matching SSM-managed instances; the possible target is the exact instance profile role, not the DLM role itself. A definite edge needs the eligible document and its code, role trust and SSM document/SendCommand grants, exact target tags, a running managed instance and its profile role. Snapshot sharing transfers data, not principal authority. The retired DLM route remains a candidate until these cross-service facts are joined.

UpdateCluster can replace a DocumentDB Elastic PLAIN_TEXT administrator password; using it still requires endpoint, username and VPC reachability. This reaches a database identity and may disrupt applications, with no second AWS IAM principal or role session. No principal edge is justified.

Reviewed PutResourcePolicy, DeleteResourcePolicy and the data-stream cross-reference. The active aws-dynamodb-putresourcepolicy-self-getitem route joins an exact active table using AWS-owned encryption and a same-account IAM user with effective PutResourcePolicy, absent prior GetItem and no surviving explicit deny. A table-policy Deny can be removed by the replacement policy. It records only newly obtainable GetItem, not a read of any item; AWS-managed or customer-managed KMS tables need a separate key-authorization join. DeleteResourcePolicy removes a resource policy but needs another Allow to change access; the stream heading is data access. Focused positive and rejection tests pass; AWS DynamoDB resource-policy authorization, supported-actions and encryption docs.

Both documented headings read EBS snapshot blocks or create a snapshot. Snapshot contents may contain credentials, but no exact credential subject, validity or IAM role is identified by either API; both are data-access routes pending content-specific proof.

Read all eight headings. The service introduction is descriptive and excluded; the only principal path is CreateComponent plus StartImagePipelineExecution against one collected pipeline, recipe component and instance-profile role. The active route checks those joins, rejects a fully pinned build and leaves narrow fixed-build grants or unreadable recipes unresolved. Current AWS semantic-versioning documentation confirms x.x.x, 1.x.x, 1.2.x and version-only 1.2.3 references can resolve to later versions/builds, while a four-node build ARN is fixed. The Service Authorization Reference confirms StartImagePipelineExecution does not require PassRole. Focused positive, negative and historical-binding tests are recorded in technique-status.tsv.

The page describes role launch, profile change, user-data execution, Auto Scaling, Spot and Instance Connect paths. Four retired EC2 routes remain candidates needing exact host, image or task-placement evidence. Active routes include current checked profile association, user-data and launch-template joins, while RunInstances still needs current sign-off; Spot and Instance Connect now preserve possible routes as unresolved until the launch or host-access facts are joined. Six related VPN entries were separately verified as network-plane effects, not IAM principal edges.

Eight retired ECR routes are conditional candidates. Image pull alone needs a verified IAM credential subject; image or repository mutation needs an exact image, mutable tag, consumer workload role and refresh path. The page also covers ECR Public and pull-through-cache variants; their service-specific account and policy prerequisites remain for implementation review.

Reviewed task definition creation and role passing, RunTask/StartTask/service paths, ECR tag refresh, node escape, ECS Exec, SSM host sessions, task sets, capacity providers, ECS Anywhere and scheduled/steered tasks. Seven catalog routes already cover bounded direct task/service and node paths; four retired ECS entries remain candidates requiring an exact connected host, running exec agent or future task placement joined to the target role. The mutable ECR consumer path is tracked under retired ECR entries. AWS ECS task, ECS Exec, ECS Anywhere and placement docs. The retired ExecuteCommand route is now restored with exact live task, container-agent, two-resource IAM and task-role SSM channel joins; the remaining ECS page routes still require review.

Read all five headings. The ECS introduction is descriptive and excluded; the sole principal route is agent impersonation from a container-instance role to task or execution-role credentials of tasks on the same EC2 host. The active YAML joins collected host placement and exact role ARNs, rejects another host and keeps the source host-role session and ACS reachability conditional; focused tests cover both role kinds, Fargate/no-host negatives and missing placement. AWS ECS task-role documentation explicitly warns that EC2 co-located containers may access credentials of other tasks or the instance role. No additional independent route appears on this page.

Reviewed full page against AWS EFS IAM/NFS access docs and active aws-efs-putfilesystempolicy-self-grant. PutFileSystemPolicy can grant exact ClientMount to the named IAM principal and is cataloged with accepted-policy and before/after authorization joins. DeleteFileSystemPolicy restores anonymous network-based NFS access, not another principal; an actual mount still needs network reachability and NFS permissions. No other principal-to-principal route on the page.

Reviewed access-entry policy and custom-group routes, Pod Identity creation/update/role chaining, node-group and Fargate creation, and the additional OIDC issuer and existing-entry sections. Existing catalog routes cover exact managed-policy association and access-entry mode changes. Six retired routes from this page are now candidates: custom groups need the same-cluster Kubernetes RBAC join, Pod Identity needs source control of the exact pod/service account and role trust, and node creation needs source control of its runtime. Creating AWS mappings alone does not give the caller another role session. AWS EKS access-entry, Pod Identity and node-group docs.

Three retired routes are candidates needing exact environment-to-instance-profile and source-bundle or runtime-execution joins. The one active PassRole create-environment route has only older sign-off and approximates dependent service permissions at Resource=*. Corrected the page's version-label mismatch, unnecessary public s3:* bucket policy and automatic rebuild-execution claim; AWS requires same-Region readable source bundle and rebuild recreates resources from the deployed application version.

The page delegates ModifyUser to the ElastiCache post-exploitation page. AWS documents password and access-string changes to a Valkey/Redis user; this is a cache data-plane identity, not an IAM principal. Exact stored credentials would need separate content evidence.
Existing-cluster AddJobFlowSteps now joins the collected cluster instance profile to its exact IAM role. Other EMR privilege-escalation sections still need individual review.

GetSessionEndpoint is a candidate direct pivot through a specific live Spark Connect session, but session ID, active state, execution role, authorization and endpoint connectivity are not collected. UpdateApplication is a conditional future-job route requiring a stopped or created application, readable controlled archive, compatible run and retained defaults; the page now states those prerequisites. Existing StartJobRun and managed-endpoint routes have only older sign-off and need current revalidation. AWS GetSessionEndpoint, Spark Connect, UpdateApplication and default-configs docs.

The linked workflow uses a passed service role for fixed Glue/S3/KMS input and S3 output operations. AWS CreateMatchingWorkflow records roleArn and typed input/output configuration; it neither returns role credentials nor runs caller code. The bounded data-movement risk is real, but not another-principal authority.

The sole StartPipe heading resumes an existing stopped pipe using its stored role, source and target. AWS StartPipe and DescribePipe show that the call neither changes the configuration nor returns role credentials; starting is asynchronous and requires eligible records plus effective source, enrichment and target access for any effect. The page now states these limits and cites the relevant Pipes docs. No other heading adds a route.

Reviewed the full page against AWS Pipes creation, execution-role and error-handling documentation. CreatePipe or UpdatePipe with PassRole can cause only configured source, enrichment and target calls; creation is asynchronous, source access is checked after creation, and records plus effective source/target permissions are required for any effect. The page now states those limits and no longer claims that source and target existence go unvalidated at creation. The generic full-role edge remains a candidate for an exact downstream authority join, not an asserted role takeover.

Reviewed six routes: fixed Lambda targets, bus self-publishing, disabled-rule reenablement and archive replay depend on existing code/events and do not by themselves yield another principal; API Destination redirects third-party credentials only. The enhanced-bus universal-target PassRole route is active and bounded by exact bus/subscriber authorization, supported target API and delivery-role permissions. No retired cohort row on this page.

Reviewed the sole route against AWS UpdateExperimentTemplate, StartExperiment, FIS Systems Manager actions and service authorization. Omitting roleArn can retain the template's existing FIS role; the SSM Automation action accepts documentArn and documentParameters, and its execution role needs FIS-role iam:PassRole. The old full-FIS-role target remains excluded: the narrower candidate needs the exact template and action authorization, document body and accepted parameters, Automation role, effective policy change and target principal before it can identify a principal-to-principal edge. The API start response does not establish execution or effect. AWS FIS API and Actions references.

Read all seven headings and the role-bearing paragraphs. The active CreateBuild plus CreateFleet route models a new controlled EC2 build with exact GameLift PassRole and same-Region actions; the existing GetComputeAccess route joins an active EC2 fleet and compute to its InstanceRoleArn with SHARED_CREDENTIAL_FILE. RequestUploadCredentials is scoped upload authority, and CreateGameServerGroup passes a FleetIQ management role rather than the instance profile. CreateContainerFleet and CreateFleet with an existing controlled artifact are separate conditional candidates recorded in additional-technique-status.tsv; neither is claimed as covered by the active new-build route. AWS CreateContainerFleet, CreateGameServerGroup, CreateFleet and GetComputeAccess docs.

AdminShell now joins one collected live session, exact RoleArn, ACTIVE parent group and effective CreateStreamSessionAdminShell authorization on that group; missing or non-ACTIVE group state gives no confirmed role edge. AWS admin-shell and ListStreamGroups docs support the new condition; direct positive and negative checks pass.
